todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.

validation.evidence: 32 tests, 0 failures. Proves explicit removal completion and accepted return/event behavior, manual/root/reply follow cleanup facts, duplicate and replay idempotency, remove/re-add/follow safety, unrelated/shared-access preservation, lag blocking, and system-group no-ops.

36 tests, 0 failures. Proves aggregate cleanup tokens can clear projection-only reply auto-follows, preserve later follows, retain composed access, and prevent a lag-hidden old follow from resuming after club rejoin.

notes: The selected stale-ordering mechanism uses each durable Membership removal event ID as a cleanup token recorded by ConversationUnfollowed in the root conversation-follow aggregate. The token emits an authoritative unfollow even when a reply auto-follow exists only in the projection; replaying the old removal is then a no-op after a post-re-add follow. Public custom-group add/remove calls wait for the origin-replaying cleanup handler, and cleanup waits for Message/access/follow projections through the removal checkpoint before discovering conversations. It excludes the removed group when checking authoritative surviving access, preserving unrelated and genuinely shared follows. The initial TDD run failed on the absent cleanup_id contract; superseded diagnostic focused runs exposed and corrected the old projection-lag test's false-success expectation and its stopped-handler test setup.
